clue.text: Area south of an island state

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece south of another is written below it, so it comes after

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A geography note placing some region below an island somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' in a down clue puts A after IOW (the Isle of Wight).
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Loves to have energy flowing slowly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves give two Os
zing is liveliness or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone who loves things gets a boost of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid seeping out gradually is oozing, a synonym for slow flow.

clue.text: Is Robert recycling space junk?

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A question whether a man named Robert is reusing discarded bits of spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead satellites and probes circling the Earth are orbiters that have become debris, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ordered militants to adopt song in advocacy of tyranny

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
put in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Militants are commanded to take up an anthem promoting despotism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link before 'adopt' but belongs to the anagram under 'Ordered'; 'adopt' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalitarianism is the doctrine supporting absolute, oppressive state control, which is advocating tyranny.

clue.text: Wrangle over goods with robust packaging

indicators.note: packaging wraps round something, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust
G is good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: A dispute about merchandise sent out in sturdy boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to argue over a price, a kind of wrangling.

clue.text: Mad extremist interrupting Liberal Democrat, missing answer

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: liberal in the sense of generous or unrestricted, free

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a Nazi is used loosely for a far-right extremist

explanation.surface: A fanatic heckling a Lib Dem politician, but without a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Democrat' reads as the party but splits into two words; 'missing' and 'interrupting' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied behaviour is wild and frantic, a synonym for mad.

clue.text: Somehow alter Vogue article re passage

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of rearranging, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An instruction to change a fashion magazine's piece about a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelogue is a piece of writing about a journey, so an article concerning passage.

clue.text: Horologer put out by a tendency to verbosity

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A clockmaker is annoyed by someone's habit of talking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is excessive wordiness, a compulsion to talk at length.

clue.text: Excellent results at risk, even when "firsts" are considered

indicators.note: firsts being considered means taking only the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Top grades are in danger, even counting first-class degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firsts' looks like university degrees but tells you to take initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean unusually fine or excellent, as in a rare talent.

clue.text: Chap getting short tart to go round Roman building

parts.note: Basil is a man's name

indicators.note: going round turns something about, so the letters are read backwards
short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tart means sour, acid

explanation.surface: A man takes a small pastry around an ancient building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' suggests pastry but means sour; 'short' and 'to go round' work on it in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong hall of ancient Rome, later a type of church.

clue.text: Retaliate about relocating grand European city

indicators.note: relocating means shifting position, so one letter is moved
about means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to avenge is to take revenge, to retaliate
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Taking revenge over moving a large Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AVENGE into EGNEVA; 'relocating' moves its G to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a major Swiss city on Lake Geneva in Europe.

clue.text: Culmination of self-inflicted damage in a slash?

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: slash is British slang for urinating, a pee
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal, damage done to one's own side

explanation.surface: A self-harming wound described as the peak of a knife slashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slash' and 'pee' are both British slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point, the climax or peak of something.

clue.text: Writers backed chief out to retire with deal?

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: No. 1, written NOI, is the chief or top one
off means away or out, as in a light that is off

explanation.surface: Authors turned their boss out so he could retire on terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To pension someone off is to make them retire with a settlement, hence 'with deal'.

clue.text: Difficult to believe credit will be cut, or hard to swallow?

indicators.note: being cut means removed, so those letters come out

parts.note: unbelievable, incredible
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An unbelievable claim that credit will be reduced, a tough pill to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to swallow' sounds figurative here but is literal about food.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inedible cannot be eaten, literally hard to swallow.

clue.text: Now dating, Ian's heady, all in a flutter

indicators.note: in a flutter means agitated and scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman is currently going out with Ian, giddy and excited.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at present, in modern times.

clue.text: Almost let US state host Tokyo's first emperor

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to let a property is to hire it out

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Ohio is a state of the USA

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Almost renting out an American state to host a Japanese ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' means rent out here; 'Almost' trims it, and 'host' wraps the state round a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirohito was Emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989.

clue.text: Escape into fresh flora in the open air

indicators.note: into places one piece within another
fresh means new, so these letters are formed anew

parts.note: ESC is the Escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Getting away among the flowers and fresh air outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' scrambles the flowers into ALFRO; 'Escape' is the computer key.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is borrowed from Italian, describing things done outdoors.

clue.text: Duke standing by national PM

indicators.note: standing by means alongside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: an Israeli is a national of Israel

explanation.surface: A nobleman supporting a citizen of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Please destroy organ

parts.note: to end something is to finish it off
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A polite request to wreck a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite opener but is a verb, to charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone fond, so to please or charm them.

clue.text: Very little gun clip?

parts.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all, so FA is very little
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A tiny firearm's ammunition magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip' looks like a gun's magazine but is the verb to attach. Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip things together is to fasten or secure them.

clue.text: Tree-lined part of Dracula's birthplace

indicators.note: part of means just a section of the word is taken

parts.note: Count Dracula came from Transylvania in Romania

explanation.surface: A wooded section of the vampire count's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvan means relating to woods, so wooded or tree-lined.

clue.text: Whipped top off and proceeded with caution

indicators.note: top off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: whipped in the slang sense of stolen, pinched

explanation.surface: Someone whisked the lid off then moved carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move very slowly and carefully, a little at a time.

clue.text: Gratuitous enmity, extremely seditious

parts.note: needle is hostility or bad feeling, as in a needle match

indicators.note: extremely takes the end letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Pointless hostility, very rebellious in nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuitous means uncalled for, unnecessary.

clue.text: Left out of stylish attempt

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: sleek means smart and stylish

explanation.surface: Abandoning a fashionable try.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek to do something is to try or attempt it.

clue.text: With which dials can be fine- tuned on screen

definitions.text: With which dials can be fine- tuned on screen

parts.words: With which dials can be fine- tuned on screen
parts.note: dials is slang for faces; a police composite picture lets a face be adjusted on a computer

explanation.surface: Describes a device whose knobs are adjusted on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dials' looks like knobs but is slang for faces.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-fit is an electronic facial composite, assembled on screen from witness descriptions.

clue.text: Hung out with old spies tailing fool they'd regularly missed

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so these come after

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: regularly missed means every other letter is skipped

explanation.surface: A man spent time with former agents who followed an idiot but lost track of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missed' drops H and Y from THEYD, leaving TED.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate with people is to keep company or socialise with them.
